You create headings by placing one or more `#` symbols at the beginning of a line, followed by a space and the heading text. ## Basic Syntax ```markdown # Heading 1 ## Heading 2 ### Heading 3 #### Heading 4 ##### Heading 5 ###### Heading 6 ``` This renders as: # Heading 1 ## Heading 2 ### Heading 3 #### Heading 4 ##### Heading 5 ###### Heading 6 ## What the Number of `#` Means The number of `#` symbols determines the heading level. | Markdown | Level | Typical Use | |---|---:|---| | `#` | Heading 1 | Main title | | `##` | Heading 2 | Major section | | `###` | Heading 3 | Subsection | | `####` | Heading 4 | Smaller subsection | | `#####` | Heading 5 | Minor section | | `######` | Heading 6 | Lowest-level heading | ## Example ```markdown # My Project ## Introduction This is the introduction. ## Features ### Login Users can log in. ### Search Users can search. ## Conclusion This is the end. ``` This would be displayed like: # My Project ## Introduction This is the introduction. ## Features ### Login Users can log in. ### Search Users can search. ## Conclusion This is the end. ## Rules ### Use a space after the `#` Most Markdown renderers require a space after the hashes. Good: ```markdown # Title ``` Less reliable: ```markdown #Title ``` ### Do not skip levels too often Instead of: ```markdown # Title ##### Subsection ``` Prefer: ```markdown # Title ## Major Section ### Subsection ``` This makes your document easier to read and improves accessibility. ### Use only one `#` heading in a document Typically, a document should have only one main title: ```markdown # Main Title ## Section ## Another Section ``` Instead of: ```markdown # Main Title # First Section # Second Section ``` ### You can close headings with extra `#` symbols Some Markdown renderers allow closing hashes: ```markdown # Title # ## Section ## ### Subsection ### ``` This is optional and not required. ## Headings vs. Bold Text A heading is not just bold text. It gives structure to your document. This is a heading: ```markdown ## Important Section ``` This is bold text: ```markdown **Important Section** ``` Headings help organize content into an outline. Bold text is usually used for emphasis inside paragraphs. ## Simple Rule Use headings like this: ```markdown # Main Title ## Main Section ### Subsection #### Small Subsection ``` So if your document is an article, report, README, notes, or webpage outline, think of the headings as the table of contents. 2. **What does `#` mean in programming?** In programming, `#` can mean different things depending on the language or context. ## 1. Comment character In many languages, `#` starts a comment. Everything after it on the same line is ignored by the program. ### Python ```python # This is a comment print("Hello") # This is also a comment ``` ### Ruby ```ruby # This is a comment puts "Hello" ``` ### Perl ```perl # This is a comment print "Hello\n"; ``` ### Shell / Bash ```bash # This is a comment echo "Hello" ``` ### R ```r # This is a comment print("Hello") ``` In these cases, `#` simply means: **“Ignore the rest of this line.”** --- ## 2. Shebang At the very beginning of a script, `#!` is called a **shebang**. Example: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env python3 print("Hello") ``` This tells the operating system which program should run the script. Examples: ```bash #!/bin/bash ``` ```bash #!/usr/bin/env python3 ``` ```bash #!/usr/bin/env ruby ``` The `#!` line is usually only allowed as the first line of a file. --- ## 3. Preprocessor directive in C and C++ In C and C++, `#` is used for **preprocessor directives**. Examples: ```c #include ``` This tells the preprocessor to include the `stdio.h` header file. ```c #define MAX 100 ``` This defines a macro. ```c #ifdef DEBUG printf("Debug mode"); #endif ``` This is conditional compilation. Common C/C++ preprocessor directives: ```c #include #define ifdef ifndef else endif pragma error warning ``` So in C/C++, a line starting with `#` is not normal C/C++ code. It is processed before the main compiler compiles the program. --- ## 4. C# language name The language **C#** uses `#` as part of its name. C# is pronounced **“C sharp”**. In C# code, `#` is also used for preprocessor directives: ```csharp #if DEBUG Console.WriteLine("Debug"); #endif ``` ```csharp #region MySection // code #endregion ``` ```csharp #pragma warning disable 0168 ``` But the `#` symbol itself is not an operator in normal C# expressions. --- ## 5. Macro stringizing and concatenation in C/C++ In C and C++ macros, `#` and `##` have special meanings. ### Stringizing ```c #define STRINGIFY(x) #x int main() { int value = 42; printf(STRINGIFY(value)); } ``` This prints: ```text value ``` The `#x` turns the macro argument into a string literal. ### Concatenation ```c #define MAKE_NAME(a, b) a ## b int main() { int my_var = 10; printf("%d", my_var); } ``` Here, `##` joins two tokens together. This is an advanced C/C++ preprocessor feature. --- ## 6. Anchor or fragment in URLs In web programming, `#` is used to refer to a part of a page.
